maker.purpose: The owner's name printed across the mat on the home page, the h1. Archivo wide 125, 900, capitals, sized to the column: two lines on a phone, one from 768px.

display.purpose: The title of every page but Home. Archivo wide 115, 800.

headline.purpose: Section and exhibit headings, the request builder's heading. Archivo wide 115, 800.

name.purpose: The term in a ruled row and a job's name in a list. Archivo wide 120, 700.

body.purpose: Everything read, at normal width, 17px. Prose caps its measure at 58 to 60ch.

lead.purpose: The paragraph under a page title, in chalk-dim.

label.purpose: Condensed capitals for what is printed small on a device or along a ruler. Never above a heading; never letter-spaced in Arabic or Kurdish, where it is 0.88rem instead.

money.purpose: IBM Plex Mono for every figure on the till and its receipt, always left to right. Used nowhere else.

rtl-display.purpose: Noto Kufi Arabic for anything set in the display class, with opened leading and no tracking.

rtl-body.purpose: Noto Sans Arabic for reading text in Arabic and Kurdish Sorani, at line-height 1.85.

shadows.name: shadow-device
shadows.purpose: Every device standing flat on the mat: browser frames, device screens, the viewer, the till, the request phone, the command menu.

shadows.name: contact
shadows.value: radial-gradient(closest-side, rgb(var(--drop) / calc(0.62 * var(--drop-k))), rgb(var(--drop) / calc(0.32 * var(--drop-k))) 55%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: The soft shadow under a 3D device on the bench, lying flat on the floor.

shadows.name: back-panel
shadows.purpose: The About plate's graphite back panel.

shadows.name: bezel-rim
shadows.purpose: The edge of a graphite device body.

shadows.name: backdrop
shadows.purpose: The bench dimmed behind the open command menu.

shadows.name: drop
shadows.purpose: The colour and strength every device shadow takes, so shadows soften on the light bench.

shadows.name: light-pool
shadows.purpose: body::before on the light bench: the lamp's pool of warm light, fixed, under everything on the mat.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Things arriving: view-transition morphs, the lamp lighting, the command menu set down.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: The default, at 200ms: colour changes and small moves; the receipt printing; the viewer resizing.

motion.name: ease-set-down
motion.purpose: Something put down on the mat: overshoots a little and settles.

motion.name: motion-gate
motion.purpose: Set before first paint unless reduced motion is asked for or Effects is off; switched off if the page has not hydrated in 8s, and back on as the visitor has it if the bundle arrives after that. Every animation hangs off it. Nothing loops.

motion.name: bench-set-down
motion.purpose: The three devices set down on the mat when first drawn.

motion.name: bench-lift
motion.purpose: A device pointed at, focused or chosen.

motion.name: bench-tilt
motion.value: damped spring, pull 0.07, damping 0.74, at most 4deg by 7deg
motion.purpose: The bench leaning under a mouse; stops when it settles.

motion.name: exhibit-morph
motion.purpose: A bench device's screen growing into its exhibit.

motion.name: project-morph
motion.purpose: The Qasa card on Projects and the Qasa page's till carried across.

motion.name: language-mirror
motion.value: old: rotateY to 90deg, 180ms cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.75, 0); new: from -90deg, 260ms ease-out-expo after 180ms; perspective 1600px; turn reversed in RTL
motion.purpose: Switching language turns the page over like a mirror.

motion.name: lamp-light
motion.value: clip-path circle from the bulb; on 560ms ease-out-expo; off 420ms cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.75, 0) reversed
motion.purpose: The lit page grows out of the bulb or shrinks back into it; colours change at once while it runs.

motion.name: ruler-read
motion.purpose: A 3 by 16px ruler mark along the header ticks, from 768px; driven by scroll, so the same with motion off.

motion.name: receipt-print
motion.purpose: The receipt fed out of the printer slot.

motion.name: till-line
motion.value: new line: opacity and -6px, 260ms ease-out-quart; quantity bump: scale 1.35, 260ms ease-set-down
motion.purpose: A line rung up, a quantity changed.

motion.name: viewer-resize
motion.value: 420ms ease-out-quart; language wipe 420ms from the reading start; site fade 260ms
motion.purpose: The site viewer changing size, language or site.

motion.name: teardown-open
motion.purpose: The computer opening and its parts sliding out.

motion.name: command-set-down

narrative.overview:
The site is a self-healing cutting mat seen from above, the kind used both for trimming print and for repairing electronics. The mat's printed grid is the page's layout grid. Three devices stand on it, one for each kind of work Mustafa takes on, and each is switched on and works: a laptop running real client sites, a till that rings up a sale, and an open computer to take apart. Everything the site claims, the visitor can operate.

Anything printed on the mat (headings, text, ruled rows, links, ruler marks) is chalk on green. Anything that is a device (a bezel, a screen, a phone, the till, the command menu) is graphite with a light screen, and looks the same whatever the light. A lamp over the bench lights it: the mat turns pale and what is printed on it turns green, while the devices stay as they are. The site opens on the dark bench.

Every device ends in the same place: the request builder, where the visitor's message is drawn as a chat bubble on a phone lying on the mat and sent from their own WhatsApp.
keyCharacteristics: A green cutting mat whose 24px grid is the page grid; every band and rule lands on a grid line.
Two kinds of colour: what is printed on the mat changes with the lamp; what belongs to a device never does.
Devices are built from ordinary elements with CSS 3D transforms, and their screens are real, working HTML.
One action colour, signal orange, always a fill under graphite text.
One Latin family in three widths, IBM Plex Mono for money on the till only, a kufi and a plain sans for Arabic and Kurdish.
Every device ends in a request the visitor sends from their own phone.
All motion is off unless it is both possible and wanted.

rules.name: The Lamp Split Rule
rules.body: Anything printed on the mat uses mat, mat-line, chalk, chalk-dim or ruler, and changes with the lamp. Anything that belongs to a device uses graphite, graphite-soft, silk, silk-dim, pcb, marker, signal, screen or bubble, and does not. A hex value written in a component is the same on both benches, so check it on both.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Signal orange is the one action colour, and it is always a fill under graphite text. One signal fill per group of actions; the others are outlines or text links. It is never text, on either bench.

rules.name: The Shadow Takes the Lamp Rule
rules.body: A device's shadow on the mat is --shadow-device, or rgb(var(--drop) / calc(alpha * var(--drop-k))). Never a fixed shadow colour: the same shadows soften on the pale mat.

rules.name: The Three Widths Rule
rules.body: Condensed is for what is printed small, normal is for reading, wide is for what is printed large. Width is the hierarchy tool; do not add a second Latin family. Plex Mono is the till's own face and appears nowhere else.

rules.name: The No Tracking in Arabic Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing is never applied to Arabic or Kurdish, positive or negative, and their text is never split into single letters or given a stroke. Every tracked style resets to normal under right-to-left, and any new one must do the same.

rules.name: The Latin Stays Latin Rule
rules.body: A machine string (a domain, the email address, the phone number) and a name written in Latin (the owner's name, Qasa POS, a client's name) stays in the Latin face and left to right in every language, isolated so the bidi algorithm cannot reorder it. Latin words inside an Arabic or Kurdish sentence ("Qasa", "Excel", "(POS)") are left to the Arabic face, because switching them to Archivo caused layout shift. The owner's name and the motto are never translated or transliterated.

rules.name: The Only Devices Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: A shadow means a thing standing on the mat. Text, rules, lists and links have none; a screen inside a device has none of its own.

dos: Do use mat, mat-line, chalk, chalk-dim and ruler for anything printed on the mat, and the device tokens for anything that is a device; check a hex value written in a component on both benches.
Do use signal orange only as a fill under graphite text, one per group of actions.
Do give a device's shadow the --drop colour and the --drop-k strength, so it softens on the light bench.
Do keep every band, heading and ruled row a whole number of 24px cells tall, and paint band rules rather than drawing borders.
Do hang every animation off html[data-motion="on"], run it once, and keep the page complete without it.
Do keep domains, the email address, the phone number and Latin names in the Latin face and left to right in all three languages.
Do reset letter-spacing to normal and open the leading for Arabic and Kurdish on every style that tracks or tightens Latin.
Do keep every tap target at least 44px, give every slider or drag a button alternative, and draw the focus ring on every control.
Do mirror every exhibit under right-to-left, with directional motion following the reading direction.
Do keep English, Arabic and Kurdish in step: the same sections, rows and order in each.
Do load an exhibit's code only when it comes near the screen, and keep the home page under 200KB of compressed JavaScript.
donts: Don't put a status on a project: no "live", "shipped", version numbers or "in progress".
Don't show a location for the owner, a dated timeline, courses or certificates, a skills list, technology tags, a GitHub link or a "designer" label.
Don't offer a Network Setup service.
Don't mention the Prayer Times app, the WebMCP till, GarageLog, Diyari, Steam Demo Remover or Al Rwad.
Don't present Qasa POS as a client's product: it is a sample of what can be built for a client, and Chrispy POS is the client version of it.
Don't invent facts, numbers, testimonials or pictures. A job gets a picture only when a real one is in the repository.
Don't place a small label above a heading.
Don't use WebGL, a 3D library or a smooth-scroll library, and don't add a preloader, scroll-jacking or a custom cursor.
Don't play sound without being asked.
Don't add a backend, a tracker or a request to another host at run time apart from the visitor's own WhatsApp, mail and phone links, and don't add a dependency without a stated reason.
